newsitem.title: USA: CBOT, CME say to pursue plan for one clearing unit.
newsitem.headline: CBOT, CME say to pursue plan for one clearing unit.

text.p: Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) and Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) said Thursday in a joint news release they will create a plan to consolidate the clearing functions of the two exchanges into a single entity.

At special meetings held at each exchange Wednesday, the boards voted to create a special, high-level subcommittee to devise and recommend for implementation a plan to consolidate their respective clearing functions, the exchanges said.

The 13-person subcommittee will operate under the auspices of the CBOT-CME Joint Strategic Initiatives Committee formed in January 1996 to explore ways to cut costs and promote efficiencies for the two exchanges and their members.
The subcommittee will be chaired by Nobel Laureate Merton Miller from the University of Chicago. The rest of the group will be CME and CBOT directors, members and executives.

"The time has come in our industry to move forward with joint clearing," said CBOT chairman Patrick Arbor. "The CBOT and the Merc utilize world-class clearing entities and the goal is to see what can be gained for our members and customers by merging the best of both."
"Business demands for cost reduction and operational efficiencies have made this a compelling time to pursue common clearing," said CME president Rick Kilcollin.
A CBOT spokesman said the subcommittee will meet "soon," but other details were not immediately available. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
